items.label: Sections
items.detail: The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 contains 358 sections; the Indian Penal Code, 1860 it replaced had 511.
items.attribution: According to the Ministry of Home Affairs
items.verified_text: 358. (1) The Indian Penal Code is hereby repealed.

sources.title: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (presentation)
The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Extraordinary
sources.publisher: Ministry of Law and Justice (via PRS Legislative Research)

items.label: Chapters
items.detail: The Act as published in the Gazette is arranged in 20 chapters, from Chapter I (Preliminary) to Chapter XX (Repeal and Savings); the Ministry compares this with 23 chapters in the IPC.
items.attribution: According to the Ministry of Home Affairs

sources.title: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (presentation)
The Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023 (Act No. 45 of 2023), Gazette of India, Extraordinary
sources.publisher: Ministry of Law and Justice (via PRS Legislative Research)

items.note: Some secondary publications describe the BNS as having 19 chapters, apparently not counting Chapter XX; the Gazette text has 20. The Delhi Police Academy handbook describes the IPC as having '23 + 3' chapters, reflecting chapters inserted into the IPC by later amendments (e.g. Chapter VA).

items.label: In force from
items.detail: The Act came into force on 1 July 2024, except sub-section (2) of section 106.
items.attribution: According to the Ministry of Home Affairs
items.verified_text: It shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint, and different dates may be appointed for different provisions of this Sanhita.

items.label: Offences punishable with community service
items.detail: Community service is added to the list of punishments in section 4 and is provided for six offences: public servant unlawfully engaging in trade, non-appearance in response to a proclamation, attempt to commit suicide to compel or restrain a public servant, first-time petty theft on restoration of property, misconduct in public by a drunken person, and defamation.
items.attribution: According to the Ministry of Home Affairs
items.verified_text: 4. … (f) Community Service. / 356(2) … or with fine, or with both, or with community service.

items.note: The Delhi Police Academy handbook cites the petty-theft provision as 'u/s 302 BNS'; in the Act text it is the proviso to section 303(2). The PIB presentation of May 2024 lists five of these situations, omitting section 209. The words 'or with community service' appear in sections 202, 209, 226 and 355, and section 303(2) provides that the offender 'shall be punished with community service'.

items.label: 'Gender' includes transgender
items.detail: The definition of 'gender' refers to any person, whether male, female or transgender.
items.attribution: According to the Ministry of Home Affairs
items.verified_text: “gender”.—The pronoun “he” and its derivatives are used of any person, whether male, female or transgender.

items.label: IPC sedition offence not reproduced
items.detail: The BNS does not contain the IPC offence of sedition (section 124A); it contains an offence of acts endangering the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India (section 152).
items.verified_text: Whoever, purposely or knowingly, … excites or attempts to excite, secession or armed rebellion or subversive activities, or encourages feelings of separatist activities or endangers sovereignty or unity and integrity of India …

items.note: The word 'sedition' does not appear in the BNS text. PRS notes that the new offence may retain aspects of the sedition offence.

items.label: Adultery and IPC section 377 not retained
items.detail: The BNS does not include the IPC offences of adultery (IPC section 497) and intercourse 'against the order of nature' (IPC section 377).

items.note: Verified by absence: neither 'adultery' nor 'order of nature' occurs in the Act text. PRS notes that omitting section 377 also removes the offences of rape of men and bestiality that it had covered.

groups.note: Official figures differ between releases: the English PIB release of the Home Minister's Lok Sabha reply on 20 December 2023 gave 21 new offences, imprisonment increased in 41, fines increased in 82, a mandatory minimum in 25, community service in 6 and 19 sections repealed; the Hindi release of the same reply gave 20 new offences, a mandatory minimum in 23, community service in 6 and 19 repealed.

items.label: Murder by a group on identity grounds
items.detail: Murder by a group of five or more persons acting in concert on grounds such as race, caste or community, sex, place of birth, language or personal belief is punishable with death or imprisonment for life; the Government describes this as the offence of mob lynching.
items.attribution: According to the Ministry of Home Affairs
items.verified_text: When a group of five or more persons acting in concert commits murder on the ground of race, caste or community, sex, place of birth, language, personal belief or any other similar ground each member of such group shall be punished with death or with imprisonment for life …

items.label: Hit-and-run provision held back
items.detail: Section 106(2), which provides up to ten years' imprisonment for causing death by rash and negligent driving and escaping without reporting it, was excluded from the 1 July 2024 commencement after a nationwide strike by transporters and drivers in January 2024.
items.verified_text: … and escapes without reporting it to a police officer or a Magistrate soon after the incident, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description of a term which may extend to ten years …

items.label: Organised crime
items.detail: Organised crime, including continuing unlawful activity such as kidnapping, extortion, land grabbing, contract killing, economic offences and cyber-crimes on behalf of a crime syndicate, has been added as an offence.
items.attribution: According to the Ministry of Home Affairs
items.verified_text: Any continuing unlawful activity including kidnapping, robbery, vehicle theft, extortion, land grabbing, contract killing, economic offence, cyber-crimes, …

items.label: Petty organised crime
items.detail: Petty organised crime, covering acts such as theft, snatching, cheating and selling of public examination question papers by a member of a group or gang, has been added as an offence.
items.attribution: According to the Ministry of Home Affairs
items.verified_text: Whoever, being a member of a group or gang, either singly or jointly, commits any act of theft, snatching, cheating, unauthorised selling of tickets, unauthorised betting or gambling, selling of public examination question papers or any other similar criminal act, is said to commit petty organised crime.

items.label: Terrorist act
items.detail: A terrorist act has been added as an offence; an officer not below the rank of Superintendent of Police decides whether to register a case under this section or under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967.
items.attribution: According to the Ministry of Home Affairs
items.verified_text: … the officer not below the rank of Superintendent of Police shall decide whether to register the case under this section or under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967.

items.label: Snatching
items.detail: Snatching has been defined as a distinct form of theft, punishable with imprisonment of up to three years and fine.
items.attribution: According to the Ministry of Home Affairs
items.verified_text: Theft is snatching if, in order to commit theft, the offender suddenly or quickly or forcibly seizes or secures or grabs or takes away from any person or from his possession any movable property.

sources.title: Key Features of the New Criminal Laws

items.label: Sexual intercourse by deceitful means
items.detail: A new offence covers sexual intercourse, not amounting to rape, obtained by deceitful means or a promise to marry made without intent to fulfil it; 'deceitful means' includes false promise of employment or promotion, or marrying by suppressing identity.
items.attribution: According to the Ministry of Home Affairs
items.verified_text: Whoever, by deceitful means or by making promise to marry to a woman without any intention of fulfilling the same, has sexual intercourse with her, such sexual intercourse not amounting to the offence of rape, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to ten years …
